DTE: the underlying, the vol curves and a vol thesis

Long 100 Nov-26 at-the-money straddles, RED book, 12–14 October 2026 (tested on 15 October). Mako BigQuery data; analysis in dte_analysis.ipynb.

DTE fell 8.5% on 9 Oct; over the next three days implied vol was priced back out (32.4% → 28.9%) while the stock realised about 22% on RED's clock, so 100 long Nov-26 straddles lost €2,822, mostly vega. Hedging frequency changes risk far more than the average. Theta should move towards the US open; a 50/50 blend of RED's clock and realised did best on 15 Oct, a day it was not built from. The vol curve's front is two events (T-Mobile US on 29 Oct, DTE on 5 Nov), each priced as a ~3.2% move and fair against history; the non-event base (25%) is about fair; skew is a steep put skew that steepened after the fall. The trade: buy the 13–20 Nov window, priced at 20%, with a gamma-neutral Nov-26 / Nov-26 W2 calendar.

1Forward curve, dividends, borrow and rolls

Forward curve (back out params, div schedule, are these stored in a different table? borrow rate), rolls market.

No dividend before the Nov-26 expiry, and borrow is negligible. Over the three days the Nov-26 forward carried at 2.75% against a 2.84% rate, leaving 9 bp for dividends plus borrow. The stored dividends (eurex_params.dividends) give RED €0.95 for April 2027 and €0.77 for April 2028, and nothing after. Rebuilt from spot, rates and those dividends, RED's 14 Oct forwards match to within €0.005 out to Jun-27; the only thing left is borrow of about 0.04%. The dividends backed out of the forwards alone (€0.96, €0.78) agree to about a cent.

On 12–13 Oct RED's forwards matched VTSTOCKS_DE's stored dividends instead (€1.05 / €1.00 / €1.00 for 2027–29); on 14 Oct they switched to RED's own, lower entries. RED's 2028 entry was last updated in May 2024. None of this touches the Nov expiries.

Theoretical rolls: +0.05 Nov→Dec, +0.19 Dec→Mar, -0.75 Mar→Jun (the dividend); no traded roll quotes were pulled.

How it's done

Carry = ln(F/S) ÷ tte; implied dividend + borrow = rate − carry; cash dividend between expiries = earlier forward grown at the forward rate minus the later forward. Stored dividends: the latest entry per book and year is the live one; each forward is rebuilt as S·e^((r−b)T) − Σ D·e^((r−b)(T−t)) and b solved.

3Realised vol

Calculate realised vol under a couple of metrics (per 30 mins, per day close-close). Calculating intraday vol? What time is open? How many real hours is the trading day? Is our entire trading day contained within 8 hrs? Annualise.

Realised was well below implied. On 30-minute returns, realised vol was 22.2% on RED's clock against implied of 29.8% on the same clock (32.4% → 28.9%). The standard 252-day annualisation gives 17.8%; close-to-close 14.3% (three returns only); one-minute numbers (19.8%, 25.0% on RED's clock) are inflated by bid/ask flicker.

Xetra opens at 09:00 and trades continuously to 17:30 CET: 8.5 hours, so the day is not contained in 8 hours; auctions before 09:00 and from 17:30 to about 17:35.

The RED-clock calculation

Implied vol is quoted per unit of RED's time to expiry (tte), which falls 0.00385 per weekday (about 1/260 of a year), of which only 64% is burned during the 8.5-hour session; the rest burns overnight. So realised vol is measured per unit of the same clock:

σ = √( Σ r² ÷ Σ ∆tte ), r = 30-minute log returns within each session, ∆tte = the tte RED burned over the same half-hours.

Over the three days: 45 returns, Σr² = 0.000304, tte burned = 0.00620 (1.61 RED days), so σ = √(0.000304 ÷ 0.00620) = 22.2%. The standard method divides the same Σr² by 45/17 sessions × 1/252 year, i.e. it treats a session as a full trading day, which gives 17.0%.

The implied number

RED's implied vol for the Nov-26 25-strike (the straddles' strike), recorded every minute in straddle_1min.csv and averaged over each day; it is also quoted on RED's clock, so it compares directly with the RED-clock realised vol. It fell from 32.4% at the 12 Oct open to 28.9% at the 14 Oct close as the 9 Oct shock was priced out.

How it's done

Standard: σ = √(mean r² × bars per day × 252). RED clock: σ = √(Σr² ÷ Σ∆tte).

4Theta decay schedule

Based on the past 3 days of market trade data, come up with a theta decay schedule.

RED's tte clock is its theta schedule: it charges 35.8% of each day's theta overnight and spreads the rest unevenly across the session. Over 12–14 Oct only two half-hours beat RED's clock on every day: 09:00 and 15:30, the open (8.3% of variance against 6.5%) and the US open (9.2% against 2.9%). Every other half-hour was above RED on some days and below on others.

Two candidate schedules, both built from 12–14 Oct only. 50/50 blend: each half-hour (and the night) gets the average of RED's share and the realised share. Anchored: RED's clock everywhere, except the half-hours where DTE moved more than RED charges on every day in the sample (09:00 and 15:30); those get their realised share, the other half-hours keep RED's relative shape scaled to fill the session, and the night keeps RED's 35.8%.

Tested on 15 Oct, a day not used to build anything. DTE gapped +2.6% overnight; the session realised 26% on RED's clock and its busiest half-hours were 09:30, 13:30 and 16:30. Share of session theta in the wrong half-hour: 50/50 blend 24.2%, RED's clock 25.6%, realised 12–14 Oct 26.0%, anchored 27.0%, flat 29.5%. The US open beat RED's clock again (6.9% of the session against 4.5%), so that pattern held on four days out of four, but the anchored schedule charges 14.9% there, inflated by one big spike on 12 Oct; its 09:00 anchor did not hold (10.0% against RED's 10.1%). Including the night every schedule misplaces more (42%–45%), because the gap alone was 80% of 15 Oct's variance.

Proposed schedule: the 50/50 blend. It did best out of sample. For the 100 straddles (€365 a day): €136 overnight, €27 at 09:00–09:30, €22 at 15:30–16:00 (RED €11), €7–€11 per half hour over lunch. The one robust finding to carry forward is the US open; one test day is one observation.

Earnings: DTE reports on 5 Nov before the open. RED's tte adds no time for it; the vol curve prices a 3.2% move, about 4 normal days (section 11). That theta belongs on the night of 4–5 Nov.

How it's done

One-minute returns in 30-minute buckets; RED share = tte burned, realised share = squared returns (moves over 1% dropped), each averaged per session and per night over 12–14 Oct. Blend: ½ RED share + ½ realised share. Anchors: half-hours where realised share > RED share on all three days. 15 Oct test: ½ Σ |schedule share − 15 Oct share|, session only and full day.

5Hedging schedule and PnL

Based on your realised vol calculations, suggest a hedging schedule and calculate PnL differences if you hedged every e.g. 10 mins vs every 3 hrs.

Actual path. The straddles lost €2,822 on the desk's theo, about €2,250 of it vega (implied fell 3.5 points as the 9 Oct shock was priced out). Hedging every 10 minutes finished at −€2,437, every 3 hours at −€1,992: 3 hours was €445 better on this one path. The cumulative chart shows why: the gap opens on a few large swings that the 3-hour hedge happened to sit through in the right direction.

What the columns mean. option: change in the straddles' value at the desk's theo, identical for every schedule. hedge: PnL on the stock hedge, the sum over minutes of (shares held × price change); being long gamma, re-hedging sells after rises and buys after falls, so it earns. costs: every share traded × €0.0064 (half the measured Xetra spread). total = option + hedge + costs. rebalances: number of hedge resets including the first; "no hedge" means hedged once at the start and never adjusted.

The simulation. One path cannot rank schedules, so 300 three-day paths were simulated on the same 1,515 timestamps. Each minute the log price moves by σ·√∆tte·Z − ½σ²∆tte (Z random normal, σ = the realised 22.2%); the overnight step uses the tte RED burns overnight, so gaps are included. The straddles are marked with Black-76 at the starting implied 32.4%, held fixed, so the simulation isolates gamma against theta and costs (no vega). Every schedule is run on every path with the same costs.

Result: averages are close (differences are mostly costs; all negative because realised 22.2% < implied 32.4%); risk is what changes: standard deviation €124 every 10 minutes, €159 hourly, €252 every 3 hours, €772 hedged once. Suggested: every 10 minutes 09:00–10:30 and 15:30–16:30, hourly otherwise (69 rebalances, standard deviation €147, €125 of costs). Hedge flat into the close before results.

7Greeks of 100 ATM straddles

Assume you are long 100x ATM straddles (go find the greeks you'd get from one of those).

Two dates: 12 Oct 2026 09:05, when the position starts (K=25, vol 32.4%, 30 trading days left), and 15 Oct 2026 (latest snapshot) (K=26, vol 28.5%).

  • Cost: €2.19 a straddle (8.8% of spot): call €1.13 + put €1.06; €21,929 for 100.
  • Delta: call +0.53, put -0.47, straddle +0.064 per share, so the position starts +635 shares (€15,877) long because the strike sits slightly below the forward. Hedged at inception.
  • Gamma: 722 shares per 1% move: after a 1% rise the position is that much longer and is re-hedged by selling. Each re-hedged 1% move earns about €90.
  • Theta: −€365 per RED day. Breakeven move: 2.01% a day; on days DTE moves more than that (re-hedged), gamma pays the theta.
  • Vega: €676 per vol point; the 3.5-point fall in implied over the window explains most of the loss in section 5.

Black-76 matches the desk (theo within €0.006, delta within 0.007). The straddle traded a median €0.28 wide (about 4.2 vol points), so a round trip in 100 costs about €2,800.

Vol curves and a vol thesis

8ATM vol in each expiry, compared

Pull ATM vol in each expiry and compare.

Out to Mar-27 ATM vol runs 25.8%–31.0%, highest in the weeklies that contain the T-Mobile US and DTE results (Nov-2026 W1 31.0%); Nov-26 28.5%, an ATM straddle at €1.90 (7.3% of the forward); Dec-26 27.1%, Mar-27 26.6%, then about 25–27% to Dec-27.

Flag: the long end fails a basic consistency check. Total variance (vol² × time) must rise with expiry, because a later option covers everything an earlier one does. It falls at Jun-2028: 18.4% at Jun-2028 gives σ²T = 0.0564, below the 0.0773 of the expiry before it, which would mean negative expected movement in between. The drop to about 18% from Jun-28 is there on every close from 8 Oct, so it is in RED's long-dated marks, not a one-day event. Those expiries are kept in every table and chart, flagged, and not used for the trade.

9Vol curves by strike: shape and skew

Pull strike vol in each expiry and plot the vol curves. What is the shape? What is the skew?

Every expiry has a downward put skew: downside strikes trade at higher vol. The short expiries, out to Nov-26, also lift the upside (a smile); from Dec-26 the upside is flat near the money. Nov-26: 90% strike 33.0%, ATM 28.7%, 110% 29.1%, a 3.9-point risk reversal. Scaled by √T the slope is about −0.04 to −0.08 from Oct-26 to Dec-27 (Sep-27 is flatter, on few strikes), so the skew is consistent along the liquid part of the curve.

After Dec-27 RED quotes 7–12 usable strikes per expiry. Their normalised slope is about -0.25, three to four times steeper than the rest of the curve, with a 90–110 risk reversal of 2.6–4.4 points around ATM levels of about 17–19%, the same low long-dated levels that fail the calendar check in section 8. Section 10 shows their skew does not change at all across five days, which suggests fixed parameters rather than live marks.

How it's done

Latest close from strike_vols_history.csv; vol at 90%/110% of the forward interpolated; quadratic fit vol(k) = a + b·k + c·k² in log-moneyness, over a range that widens with √T.

10How the vol curves changed over 5 days

Can we pull 5 days of historic strike or ATM vol data to see how the vol curve has changed?

Yes: five closes, 10-08 to 10-14. On 9 Oct DTE fell 8.5% (26.87 → 24.67).

The Nov-26 story. Before the fall (10-08) Nov-26 sat at 28.9% ATM with a 3.0-point risk reversal. On the crash day ATM jumped to 32.4%, but the upside jumped most (29.6% → 33.7%) while the downside rose less (32.6% → 35.0%): the skew flattened to 1.3 points. Uncertainty jumped in both directions, a rebound as much as a further fall. Over the next three sessions ATM and upside vol bled back (28.7% ATM, 29.1% upside) while the downside stayed near 33.0%: the skew steepened past where it started, to 3.9 points (4.8 at its peak). The market priced the crash out of ATM vol but kept paying for downside protection.

The same happened across the front (Dec-26 risk reversal 2.0 → 1.1 → 3.2). The results weeklies stayed high because the events are still ahead. From Jun-28 the risk reversal is identical on all five days.

11Forward vol curve, events, and the non-event base

Build a forward volatility curve from the ATM vols of listed expiries. Find the events calendar: are there any events scheduled? Build a non-event base forward volatility curve.

Forward vol between two expiries is the vol the market charges for that window alone: √((σ₂²T₂ − σ₁²T₁)/(T₂ − T₁)). Two weeks are priced far above the rest: 23–30 Oct at 33.9% (T-Mobile US Q3, released 28 Oct after the US close, so DTE reacts on 29 Oct) and 30 Oct–6 Nov at 34.1% (DTE Q3, 5 Nov before the open). Event-free windows sit around 25%: the non-event base is 25.1%, and each event is priced as a one-day move of about 3.2% (≈4 normal days). The non-event base forward vol curve is the market's forward curve with those two weeks set to the base.

Switching the events off one at a time (chart, bottom): Nov-26 is 28.5% with both events, 26.8% without T-Mobile, 26.7% without DTE's results, and 24.8% without both. Each event is worth about 1.8–1.8 vol points of Nov-26. Without them the curve is almost flat around 25%.

One window is priced well below the base: 13–20 Nov at 19.9%, with no event in it. The full curve (top) includes every expiry; 1 window after Dec-27 has negative forward variance (grey), the calendar-check failure from section 8.

12Realised vol over the last year, past event moves, and Mako's event pricing

Is the non-event vol cheap or rich, are the events priced right, and how does Mako price them?

Non-event vol

With past results days removed, 20/60-day realised vol looks high (39% / 31%), but almost all of that is one day, 9 Oct (-8.5%). Without it: 25.0% (20 days), 26.1% (60), 28.5% (120), 26.0% (250). The typical-day measure, which one day cannot move, is about 25%. So the 25.1% base is about fair for normal days. DTE is jumpier than a normal distribution: 19 days over 3% in the last year, which favours owning vol over selling it.

Events against history

Past DTE results days moved -0.4% (Nov 25), -1.6% (Feb 26), +0.9% (May 26), +7.1% (Aug 26): root-mean-square 3.7%, median 1.3%, against 3.2% priced. T-Mobile US results days moved DTE -2.3% (Oct 25), +5.1% (Feb 26), +1.6% (Apr 26), -4.0% (Jul 26): root-mean-square 3.5%, median 3.2%, against 3.2% priced. On the root-mean-square the events look fairly priced; on the median they look rich, because one or two big days (DTE +7.1% in Aug 2026) dominate four observations. No edge either way.

Mako's own event pricing

Mako's event table for DTE (mako_events.csv) disagrees with the sourced calendar: it holds DTE's Q3 2026 results on 13 Nov (value 2, an estimate, last updated 27 Aug 2026 by JDAVIES), while DTE's investor-relations calendar and Bloomberg both say 5 Nov. 13 Nov is last year's Q3 date. It has no T-Mobile US event, although the market prices one at about 3.2%. 11 of its 15 entries were last edited before 2025 (value 1.2, estimated dates): Q2 2026 still says 7 Aug, DTE reported on 6 Aug. The market-fitted vols put the event in the right week; the 6–13 Nov window, a little above the base, may partly reflect the misdated entry. The unit of event_value is not in the data: if it is the expected move in %, Mako's 2 is below the 3.2% the curve prices and the 3.7% DTE has averaged. Worth correcting the date, adding T-Mobile US, and confirming the unit with the desk.

13The trade

Based on this, what trade would you put on in German Telecom?

The reasoning

  1. Events: priced at about 3.2% each against 3.7% / 3.5% historically (section 12): fair, so no event trade.
  2. Base: 25.1% against 25%–26% realised on normal days: fair, so no outright long or short vol. DTE's jumps argue against selling.
  3. One window is off: 13–20 Nov is priced at 19.9%, 5.2 points below the base, with no event in it. Its neighbours are at 27.3% (the week before) and 24.9% (the month after).

The trade: buy that week with a gamma-neutral calendar

Buy 100 Nov-2026 ATM straddles (expire 20 Nov) and sell 95 Nov-2026 W2 ATM straddles (expire 13 Nov). Sizing: the ratio of the two straddles' gammas, 0.95, so that until 13 Nov a move in DTE changes both legs' deltas equally and the position barely cares where the stock goes. Everything before 13 Nov, including both results dates, sits in both legs and roughly cancels; what is left is the 13–20 Nov week.

  • Cost and greeks (table): net premium €1,770, net vega €96 per vol point, net theta €44 a day, net gamma close to zero.
  • How it makes money: if the market reprices the week to the 25.1% base, the position gains about €514. Held to 13 Nov with the stock at the strike, the short weekly expires worthless and the long monthly keeps one week of value: positive above a week vol of 6.1% (right chart). That is the carry the position earns for being short gamma near the weekly's expiry (next point).
  • How it loses: it is gamma-neutral only at inception. As both expiries approach, the short weekly's gamma grows faster than the long monthly's. By the 04 Nov close, the night before DTE's results, the position is net -255 shares per 1% move (short gamma), and a priced-size 3.2% results gap would cost about €346, which cannot be hedged overnight. To stay neutral into results, buy back weeklies to about 80 by that close (or accept the exposure). Held unhedged to 13 Nov, the left chart applies: with the week at 20% the position loses if DTE is outside about €25.45, €26.75 that day. In practice the delta is hedged daily and the ratio re-set.
  • Scale: the numbers are for 100 straddles; the trade can be sized up in the same ratio.
  • Risks: one week between neighbouring expiries is sensitive to small errors in either mark, so check the Nov W2 and Nov-26 quotes first; weeklies trade wider; skew is not hedged; a large move around the results can leave the strikes far from the money.

Data and sources

Mako BigQuery (project cloud-data-bq-p-base-919c)

  • eurex_vol.pricing_params_1min: spot (model mid), forwards, rates, tte; RED book (spot_1min_full, daily_ohlc, daily_closes, forward_curve, forward_curve_daily).
  • eurex_vol.listed_strike_1min: Nov-26 25-strike implied vol and tte every minute, 12–15 Oct (straddle_1min, test_15oct_1min); every strike at each close (strike_vols_history).
  • eurex_vol.ivol_norm_strike_1min / _t0: ATM vol per expiry (atm_history, atm_term_structure).
  • eurex_raw.theodata_snapshot + marketdepth_snapshot: desk theo, delta, bid and ask for the 25-strike call and put (straddle_quotes_1min).
  • eurex_raw.markettrade: every DTE option trade with the Xetra stock bid/ask (trades); 30-day forward backed out of option trades (fwd30_theo).
  • eurex_params.dividends: stored dividends (dividends). Mako's DTE event table (mako_events).
  • single_stocks.bbg_earnings_expected: DTE's next results date (Bloomberg).

Outside sources (events)

  • Deutsche Telekom investor-relations and media calendars (telekom.com): Q3 2026 on 5 Nov 2026, Q4/FY 2026 on 25 Feb 2027, Q1 2027 on 12 May 2027, AI Investor Day on 5 Oct 2026.
  • T-Mobile US press release (BusinessWire, 17 Sep 2026): Q3 2026 results on 28 Oct 2026 after the US close.
  • Nordnet corporate-actions calendar, Benzinga and Earnings Whispers: past DTE and T-Mobile US results dates.

Caveats

  • Three days of intraday data plus one test day; single-path results (which hedge interval won, the 15 Oct test) are single observations.
  • The price path is RED's model mid, confirmed to within a tick by Xetra quotes, but not a record of stock trades.
  • Hedging cost is half the measured Xetra spread; size and market impact ignored.
  • Event history is four results days each for DTE and T-Mobile US.
  • RED's long end (Jun-28 onward) fails the calendar check and its skew does not move; flagged, not used for the trade.
  • Mako's event table misdates DTE's Q3 results and has no T-Mobile US event; the analysis uses the sourced dates.
  • No position data (STOCKS_EUR not available).
